label: broadsheet
design: Front page of a serious newspaper. Serif throughout. A black utility bar, a centred masthead with a tagline, nav, and a dateline strip — availability, discipline, date, Troy, Ohio. Tight leading, small-caps kickers, one red spot colour. On wide viewports the front page becomes a lead-story layout: an outsized headline on the left, the dek in a ruled column beside it, then four problem columns with hairlines between them, all above the fold. Cards read as columns of a front page, not as boxes.
language: Newspaper register without the parody. Lead with the fact. A dek that adds information rather than repeating the headline. Present tense for standing facts, past for work that happened. No exclamation, no second-person selling.
use_for: Home. The one page a stranger lands on cold.
note: The front-page layout is pure CSS Grid placement on the first three children of <main>, scoped by [data-page="index"]. DOM order is untouched, so reading and focus order still run headline, dek, call to action. Single-scheme on purpose. A front page is ink on newsprint; there is no dark broadsheet to be faithful to.
